issues.title: Make LOE_ID a first-class concept instead of overloading LookupItemNumericValue
issues.description:
_Follow-up from the lookup architecture review (#398). Source: the project backlog docs._

### Problem
"LOE_ID" is stored in the generic `LookupItem.LookupItemNumericValue` column — the same column also holds FiscalYear numeric values — and the admin UI shows/edits it only when a runtime heuristic (`ViewBag.LoeIdFk_LookupID`, `LookupItemController.cs:241`) decides the current item is a LevelOfEffort item (`_EditFields.cshtml:90-104`, `_ViewFields.cshtml:62-72`). The overload is non-obvious and the gating is not tied to the `LevelOfEffort` enum constant.

### Proposed change
Lowest-cost: replace the heuristic with the explicit `eLookups.LevelOfEffort` constant so the LOE_ID field renders deterministically. Higher-value (optional): give LevelOfEffort a small extension table (`LookupItem_LevelOfEffortExt`) following the established `*Ext` pattern so LOE_ID has a named, typed home.

### Affected files
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Areas/Admin/Controllers/LookupItemController.cs`
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Areas/Admin/Views/LookupItem/_EditFields.cshtml`
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Areas/Admin/Views/LookupItem/_ViewFields.cshtml`
- (optional) new `LookupItem_LevelOfEffortExt` model + Fluent config + migration

### Rough effort
S for the heuristic-to-constant fix; M if adding the extension table.

### Severity
Med (D4)

issues.title: Adopt the VendorId mapping conventions as the standard for lookup mapping tables
issues.description:
_Follow-up from the lookup architecture review (#398). Source: the project backlog docs._

### Problem
The codebase has several lookup *mapping* tables built to different standards. The newest, `LookupItem_CageCodeToPrimeContractor` (2026-01), is the cleanest: explicit org scoping, a unique constraint (`UX_Cage_Prime_Org`), single-purpose entity. The older Service Code mapping tables (`LookupItem_PscCodeToSpendCat`, `LookupItem_PscCodeGoalMap`) lack uniqueness and lean on sprocs/magic strings. There is no written convention, so the next mapping table is likely to repeat the older mistakes.

### Proposed change
Write a short "lookup mapping table" convention doc (org-scoped FK, unique composite index, enum-backed type references, EF-LINQ-first over sprocs where practical) and add a lightweight checklist to the PR/MR template. Reference it from the review. No production code change required.

### Affected files
- New `docs/architecture/lookup-mapping-conventions.md`
- (reference) `docs/architecture/lookup-architecture-review.md`

### Rough effort
S.

### Severity
Process / convention

issues.title: Add supporting indexes for lookup foreign keys and review delete behavior
issues.description:
_Follow-up from the lookup architecture review (#398). Source: the project backlog docs._

### Problem
Lookup FK indexing is inconsistent: `LookupItem` indexes `LookupItemValue` and `fk_Lookup_ID` (`OneNListContext.cs:450-452`), but the Service Code mapping FKs and several `OneNList` lookup FK columns have no dedicated supporting index (DB-verified: `LookupItem_PscCodeToSpendCat` has only the clustered PK). Every lookup FK uses `OnDelete(ClientSetNull)` (`OneNListContext.cs:617-635`), creating orphan/null risk on lookup deletion.

### Proposed change
Audit lookup FK columns (mapping tables + `OneNList` lookup FKs) for missing nonclustered indexes and add them where the goal/mapping queries justify it. Review whether `ClientSetNull` is the right delete behavior per relationship (e.g. `Restrict` for mappings that must not be silently orphaned). Apply via Fluent config + SQL migration.

### Affected files
- `Source/OneNListApp.Data/OneNListContext.cs` (indexes + delete behavior)
- New SQL migration under `Source/Migrations/<next-version>/`

### Rough effort
M.

### Severity
Low (D6)

issues.title: feat: add selectable "Total Funded Amount" column to action list (sum all FYs)
issues.description:
Meridian has requested a selectable list-view column showing the **total funded amount across all fundings** for each action, regardless of fiscal year — restoring a column that existed before the dynamic column-selection capability. The value uses the **same data source as the existing `CurrentFyObligationAmount` column** (`OneNList_ProjectedObligation.Amount`), but sums every row for the action rather than filtering to the current FY. This mirrors the `CurrentFyObligationAmount` / `NextFyObligationAmount` pattern added in #725, plus a column-config migration so org owners can opt the column into any view. The new column must preserve the established NULL-on-empty semantics (no obligation rows → blank/`$0`, not a misleading aggregate).

**Files to modify:**

* `Source/OneNListApp.Data/StoredProcedures/Models/GetOneNListItemsByUser.cs` — add a new nullable DTO property (e.g. `TotalFundedAmt`, `[Display(Name = "Total Funded Amount")]`, `[DisplayFormat(DataFormatString = "{0:n}")]`), distinct from the existing static `TotalObligatedAmount` property.
* `Source/OneNListApp.Service/OneNListItemService.cs` — in `QueryForList`, project `TotalFundedAmt` as `SUM(OneNList_ProjectedObligation.Amount)` for the action across **all** `ObligationYear` values, guarded with `.Any()` to return `null` (not `0`) when no rows exist — mirroring the existing `CurrentFyTotalObligatedAmt` block but without the `ObligationYear == currentFy` filter. Add a unit-tested static helper `SumAllObligations(obligations)` alongside the existing `SumObligationsForFiscalYear`.
* `Source/OneNListApp.Service/ActionListColumnConfigService.cs` — add `"TotalFundedAmount"` to the canonical `ColumnKeys` list (the \~20-key registry, near `CurrentFyObligationAmount`/`NextFyObligationAmount`).
* `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Views/List/Index.cshtml` — add a `case "TotalFundedAmount":` rendering a `<td data-col-key="TotalFundedAmount">` with the same `$`/`$0` rendering used by the existing FY obligation columns.
* `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Controllers/ListController.cs` — add sort cases (`TotalFundedAmt` / `TotalFundedAmt_desc`) to the OrderBy switch, and a `["TotalFundedAmount"]` entry to the column-config sort-mapping dictionary.
* `Source/Migrations/5.1.4/05_20260618_AddTotalFundedAmountColumnConfig.sql` — **new migration**: seed `Organization_ActionList_Column_Config` rows for `TotalFundedAmount` across the same orgs/views as #725, `IsVisible=0`, `IsFilterable=0`, `FilterType='numeric'` (opt-in), `DisplayName='Total Funded Amount'` for Meridian (org JPOCompliance).

**Acceptance Criteria:**

*  A `TotalFundedAmount` column key exists and is selectable per-org/per-view in the Admin → Action List Column Config screen.
  * [ ]  When enabled, the list view shows the sum of all `OneNList_ProjectedObligation.Amount` rows for each action across every obligation year, formatted as currency.
  * [ ]  An action with no projected-obligation rows renders blank/`$0` (NULL-on-empty), consistent with the Current/Next FY columns.
  * [ ]  The column header reads "Total Funded Amount" (or the org's configured `DisplayName`); no "PO"/"JPO" text in any user-visible label.
  * [ ]  The column is sortable ascending and descending.
  * [ ]  The column is hidden by default (opt-in) until an org owner enables it.
  * [ ]  Project builds with no errors or warnings after the change.
  * [ ]  All existing tests continue to pass.

**Unit Test Requirements:**

_(Moq + MockDbSetHelper pattern in `OneNListApp.Tests/`; name as `Subject_Condition_ExpectedResult`.)_

* `OneNListItemService.SumAllObligations_MultipleFiscalYears_ReturnsSumAcrossAllYears` — asserts amounts from different `ObligationYear` values are all summed.
* `OneNListItemService.SumAllObligations_NoObligationRows_ReturnsNull` — asserts NULL (not 0) on empty set, matching the FY-column semantics.
* `OneNListItemService.SumAllObligations_SingleYear_EqualsThatYearTotal` — asserts the all-years total equals the per-FY total when only one year has rows (cross-check against `SumObligationsForFiscalYear`).

issues.title: feat: add "RFP Release Date Revised" as a selectable Action List column
issues.description:
In the **Action List Column Configuration** admin page (Admin area, Owner access), admins customize which columns appear in each action list view (Recent, **All Open Actions / PreAward**, Draft, Awarded, Cancelled, Expired, Deleted).

The customer wants the **RFP Release Date Revised** field to appear as a selectable column. Currently it is not offered as a choice.

Good news: the field already exists end-to-end in the data model (entity, view-model, item form, history/audit, exports). It simply has not been _wired in_ as a selectable list column. A non-revised **RFP Release Date** column already exists and is selectable — this ticket adds the **Revised** variant alongside it, across **all views**.

**Existing data plumbing (already present, no new schema needed):**

* Entity: `OneNList.RFPReleaseDateRevised` — [OneNList.cs:198](vscode-webview://0nfnc11nghrep6s3jh3und5rh4tbkta95dj880h1qbj3egeupg18/Source/OneNListApp.Data/Models/OneNList.cs#L198) (`DateOnly?`)
* List view-model: `GetOneNListItemsByUser.RFPReleaseDateRevised` — [GetOneNListItemsByUser.cs:240](vscode-webview://0nfnc11nghrep6s3jh3und5rh4tbkta95dj880h1qbj3egeupg18/Source/OneNListApp.Data/StoredProcedures/Models/GetOneNListItemsByUser.cs#L240) (`DateTime?`)

## Background — how a column becomes selectable

A column is only offered/displayed when its `ColumnKey` is wired into several hardcoded maps that must be kept in sync (this is why the field exists but isn't selectable today):

1. Master key list `_allColumnKeys` — [ActionListColumnConfigService.cs:14-21](vscode-webview://0nfnc11nghrep6s3jh3und5rh4tbkta95dj880h1qbj3egeupg18/Source/OneNListApp.Service/ActionListColumnConfigService.cs#L14-L21)
2. A render `case` in the List view — [Views/List/Index.cshtml:143-264](vscode-webview://0nfnc11nghrep6s3jh3und5rh4tbkta95dj880h1qbj3egeupg18/Source/OneNListApp.Web/Views/List/Index.cshtml#L143-L264)
3. A default header label — [Index.cshtml:20-42](vscode-webview://0nfnc11nghrep6s3jh3und5rh4tbkta95dj880h1qbj3egeupg18/Source/OneNListApp.Web/Views/List/Index.cshtml#L20-L42)
4. A sort-param entry — [ListController.cs:126-150](vscode-webview://0nfnc11nghrep6s3jh3und5rh4tbkta95dj880h1qbj3egeupg18/Source/OneNListApp.Web/Controllers/ListController.cs#L126-L150) (`ViewBag.ColumnSortParams`)
5. Date-range filter support — [ListFilterHelper.cs](vscode-webview://0nfnc11nghrep6s3jh3und5rh4tbkta95dj880h1qbj3egeupg18/Source/OneNListApp.Web/Helpers/ListFilterHelper.cs) (`ApplyDateRangeFilter`)
6. A seed migration so existing orgs get the new config row — mirror how `RfpReleaseDate` is seeded in `Source/Migrations/5.1.2/02_...sql` and `05_...sql`

The existing `RfpReleaseDate` column is the exact pattern to mirror.

## Acceptance Criteria

*  **RFP Release Date Revised** appears as a selectable column in the Admin Action List Column Configuration page **for all views** (Recent, PreAward / All Open Actions, Draft, Awarded, Cancelled, Expired, Deleted).
  * [ ]  The column **defaults to hidden** (`IsVisible = 0`) for every org/view — admins opt in via the configuration page.
  * [ ]  When an admin enables the column for an org/view, it renders in the List view showing `item.RFPReleaseDateRevised`.
  * [ ]  Column header label reads **"RFP Release Date Revised"** (overridable via the existing Display Name Override).
  * [ ]  Column is sortable (sort link works) consistent with other date columns.
  * [ ]  Date is displayed in **MM/dd/yyyy** date-only format, consistent with the other list date columns (NOTE: the view-model currently formats this property as `MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm` — render it date-only in the column to match `RFP Release Date` / `Award Date`).
  * [ ]  Column is **date-range filterable** (admin can enable `IsFilterable` with `FilterType = daterange`), matching the behavior of the other selectable date columns.
  * [ ]  A seed migration adds the new config row (default hidden) for **all existing organizations and all views**, so existing saved configurations are not broken.
  * [ ]  Existing organizations' current column selections are unaffected; the new column is purely additive.
  * [ ]  Unit tests cover the new column key in the service defaults, plus the render/label/sort/filter mapping.

## Implementation Notes (suggested)

Mirror the existing `RfpReleaseDate` wiring, using new key `"RfpReleaseDateRevised"` → property `item.RFPReleaseDateRevised`:

1. Add `"RfpReleaseDateRevised"` to `_allColumnKeys` ([ActionListColumnConfigService.cs:20](vscode-webview://0nfnc11nghrep6s3jh3und5rh4tbkta95dj880h1qbj3egeupg18/Source/OneNListApp.Service/ActionListColumnConfigService.cs#L20)).
2. Add a render `case` in [Index.cshtml](vscode-webview://0nfnc11nghrep6s3jh3und5rh4tbkta95dj880h1qbj3egeupg18/Source/OneNListApp.Web/Views/List/Index.cshtml#L261) (near the `RfpReleaseDate` case), **formatting date-only**.
3. Add `defaultLabels` entry → "RFP Release Date Revised" ([Index.cshtml:20-42](vscode-webview://0nfnc11nghrep6s3jh3und5rh4tbkta95dj880h1qbj3egeupg18/Source/OneNListApp.Web/Views/List/Index.cshtml#L20-L42)).
4. Add `ColumnSortParams` entry + matching sort branch in the list query/sort logic ([ListController.cs:126-150](vscode-webview://0nfnc11nghrep6s3jh3und5rh4tbkta95dj880h1qbj3egeupg18/Source/OneNListApp.Web/Controllers/ListController.cs#L126-L150)).
5. Add `case "RfpReleaseDateRevised"` to `ApplyDateRangeFilter` in [ListFilterHelper.cs](vscode-webview://0nfnc11nghrep6s3jh3und5rh4tbkta95dj880h1qbj3egeupg18/Source/OneNListApp.Web/Helpers/ListFilterHelper.cs) so date-range filtering works when enabled.
6. Add a seed migration (next version folder) inserting the new `Organization_ActionList_Column_Config` row for **every org and every view**, `IsVisible = 0`, `IsFilterable` defaulted off, mirroring the `RfpReleaseDate` seed rows in `Source/Migrations/5.1.2/02_*` and `05_*`.

## Notes for the implementer

* This is a **pure wiring task** — no new schema, since `OneNList.RFPReleaseDateRevised` already exists.
* The one real gotcha is the **format mismatch**: the view-model property is `MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm`, but every other list date column is date-only — the render `case` should format it date-only.

issues.title: feat: combine PM C&S and PM DCO into PM CW (Crestline)
issues.description:
## Description

Crestline wants the two PM/PD values **"PM C&S"** and **"PM DCO"** merged into a single value **"PM CW"**. PM/PD values are not hardcoded — they are `LookupItem` rows in the `PMPD` lookup category (`Enumerations.eLookups.PMPD`), joined to actions via `OneNList.fk_PMPD_Lookup_ID`.

The Admin → LookupItem screen (`Source/OneNListApp.Web/Areas/Admin/Controllers/LookupItemController.cs`) can Create/Edit a *single* item but has **no merge / bulk-reassign**, so combining two PMs into one must be done as an **idempotent SQL data migration** under `Source/Migrations/`, following the header/guard conventions of existing migrations (e.g. `Source/Migrations/5.1.4/02_20260610_AddNextFyObligationAmountColumnConfig.sql`). The merge must be scoped to Crestline's organization/security group so other orgs' PM lists are untouched.

## Approach (in one transaction, idempotent)

1. Resolve the surviving target: rename one existing item to **"PM CW"**, or create a new `PMPD` `LookupItem` "PM CW" if neither exists. Capture its `ID` as `@cwId` and the source IDs `@csId` (PM C&S) and `@dcoId` (PM DCO).
2. Repoint actions: `UPDATE OneNList SET fk_PMPD_Lookup_ID = @cwId WHERE fk_PMPD_Lookup_ID IN (@csId, @dcoId)`.
3. Migrate & de-dupe dependent extension rows from the source IDs to `@cwId`:
   - `LookupItem_PMPDExt` (per-security-group / `ARPCollaborationURL` assignments) — re-point `fk_LookupItem_ID`, skipping duplicates on `(fk_LookupItem_ID, fk_PMSecurityGroupID)`.
   - `LookupItem_PriorityReorderExt` (priority ordering rows).
   - `Organization_Lookup_Config` rows referencing the source IDs.
4. Retire the now-orphaned "PM C&S" and "PM DCO" items per product-owner decision (delete vs. keep inactive — see open question).
5. Verify no remaining FK references to `@csId`/`@dcoId` before deletion.

## Files to modify

- `Source/Migrations/5.1.4/<NN>_<YYYYMMDD>_CombinePmCsAndDcoIntoPmCw.sql` *(new — use the next sequence number in the current sprint folder)* — performs steps 1–5 above with `IF NOT EXISTS` guards and a `PRINT @@ROWCOUNT` summary so re-runs are no-ops.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After the migration, a single PM/PD value "PM CW" exists for Crestline; "PM C&S" and "PM DCO" no longer appear as selectable PM/PD options for Crestline users.
- [ ] Every Crestline action previously assigned to "PM C&S" or "PM DCO" is now assigned to "PM CW" (no orphaned/NULL `fk_PMPD_Lookup_ID`).
- [ ] Security-group assignments (`LookupItem_PMPDExt`), priority-reorder rows, and `Organization_Lookup_Config` entries for the old items are carried over to "PM CW" with no duplicates.
- [ ] No PM/PD values for any other organization are altered.
- [ ] Migration is idempotent: re-running produces 0 changes and no errors.
- [ ] Project builds; all existing tests continue to pass.

## Unit Test Requirements

Omitted — this is a pure data migration with no new C#/service logic. If desired, add an integration check that no `OneNList` rows reference the retired lookup IDs after migration.

## ⚠ Open questions for product owner before implementation

1. Confirm the exact current `LookupItemValue` spellings and IDs for the two items (e.g. is it literally "PM C&S" / "PM DCO"?), and which Crestline organization/security group they belong to.
2. Should the old "PM C&S" / "PM DCO" items be **hard-deleted** or **kept but hidden/inactive** for historical/audit purposes?
3. Confirm "PM CW" is the exact desired display text and whether it should inherit C&S's or DCO's existing priority position/security-group config.

issues.title: fix: Admin Lookup Item editor reads Is Direct / Is Reimbursable across all orgs (not org-scoped)
issues.description:
## Summary

Riverside reported that the **Is Direct** / **Is Reimbursable** fund-type filter on the Type of Funding form filtered out all selectable Type of Fund options. Further observation narrowed the real defect: setting the flag in Admin > Lookup Item, saving, then re-opening the **same** lookup item shows the checkbox **unchecked** — yet the Type of Fund dropdown filters correctly. So the value **is** persisted; the **Admin editor display** does not reflect it.

## Observed behavior (reporter)

> I defined the setting in the admin tools, clicked save, then re-opened the same lookup. The field did not show clicked anymore, but the dropdown list is now filtered correctly even though the setting does not appear defined in the admin section.

## Root cause

`IsDirect` / `IsReimbursable` / `RequireIncumbent` are stored **per organization** in `Organization_Lookup_Config` (`fk_LookupItem_ID` + `fk_Organization_ID`). A single lookup item has one config row **per org**. The save and display paths in `LookupItemController` are asymmetric:

- **Save (correct, org-scoped):** `LookupItemController.cs:276` calls `LookupConfigService.GetByLookupItemAsync(model.LookupItem, SessionManager.GetOrganizationId())`, which filters `x.fk_Organization_ID == organizationId` (`LookupConfigService.cs:57`). The current org's row is updated correctly — which is why the front-end Type of Fund filter (org-scoped via the `GetLookupItems` SP) now works.

- **Display / Edit GET (buggy, NOT org-scoped):** `LookupItemController.cs:221`

```csharp
var orgConfig = model.LookupItem.Organization_Lookup_Config.FirstOrDefault();
model.IsDirect = orgConfig?.IsDirect ?? false;
```

`model.LookupItem` is loaded by `LookupItemService.Find(id)` — a bare `_dbContext.Set<LookupItem>().Find(id)` with no `Include` and no org filter (`LookupItemService.cs:79`). Accessing the `Organization_Lookup_Config` navigation lazy-loads **all** rows for that lookup item across **every** organization, and `FirstOrDefault()` (no `Where`, no ordering) returns an arbitrary org's row — typically another org whose flag is null/false. The current org's saved value is therefore not displayed, so the checkbox appears unchecked / undefined.

## Fix

- **Primary** — `LookupItemController.cs:221`: load the current org's config explicitly instead of the unscoped navigation `FirstOrDefault()`. Use the existing org-scoped service, e.g.:

```csharp
var orgConfig = (await LookupConfigService.GetByLookupItemAsync(model.LookupItem, SessionManager.GetOrganizationId())).FirstOrDefault();
```

  (or `LookupConfigService.GetByLookupItemIdAsync(model.LookupItem.ID, SessionManager.GetOrganizationId())`, which already returns a single org-scoped row — `LookupConfigService.cs:61`).

- **Save update branch hardening** — `LookupItemController.cs:277` resolves `orgConfigs` the same unscoped way (`model.LookupItem.Organization_Lookup_Config.FirstOrDefault()`) before falling back to the org-scoped `lookup.FirstOrDefault()`. It works today only because the model-bound nav collection is empty on POST. Make it use the org-scoped result directly to avoid editing/duplicating the wrong org's row if that ever changes.

- **Latent (separate) defect** — `LookupItemController.cs:299` (insert branch) sets `orgConfigs.fk_Organization_ID = SessionManager.GetUserId();` instead of `GetOrganizationId()`. This is not the reported symptom (the update branch handles existing rows), but it will mis-key a brand-new config row to a user id. Fix while here.

## Files to modify

- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Areas/Admin/Controllers/LookupItemController.cs` — line 221 (org-scope the display read); line 277 (org-scope the save read); line 299 (`GetUserId()` -> `GetOrganizationId()`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Set Is Direct (and/or Is Reimbursable) on a Type of Fund lookup item in Admin > Lookup Item, save, re-open the same item: the checkbox reflects the saved value for the current organization.
- [ ] The displayed flags reflect only the **current org's** `Organization_Lookup_Config` row, regardless of other orgs' rows for the same lookup item.
- [ ] Saving does not create a duplicate or modify another org's `Organization_Lookup_Config` row.
- [ ] A newly inserted config row (first-time flag on an item with no existing row) is keyed to the organization id, not a user id.
- [ ] The Type of Funding Is Direct / Is Reimbursable dropdown filter continues to work for Riverside.
- [ ] Project builds with no errors or warnings; all existing tests pass.

## Unit Test Requirements

*(Follow the Moq + MockDbSetHelper pattern in `OneNListApp.Tests/`.)*

- `LookupItemController.Edit_Get_WhenItemHasConfigsForMultipleOrgs_DisplaysCurrentOrgFlags` — lookup item with `Organization_Lookup_Config` rows for org A (IsDirect=true) and org B (IsDirect=false); session org = A; assert `model.IsDirect == true`.
- `LookupItemController.Edit_Post_WhenNoExistingOrgConfig_InsertsConfigWithOrganizationId` — assert inserted row's `fk_Organization_ID == GetOrganizationId()`.
- `LookupItemController.Edit_Post_UpdatesOnlyCurrentOrgConfigRow` — assert the current org's row is updated and other orgs' rows are untouched.

issues.title: Admin: Type of Funding section shows no fields — display names cannot be edited
issues.description:
## Summary
The Admin > Form Field Settings > Financials > **Type of Funding Settings** page (`/Admin/Field/Section?Section=TypeOfFunding`) renders an empty field table. No fields are listed, so an admin cannot edit the display names (or other field settings) for the Type of Funding section.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Log in as an Owner.
2. Go to Admin > Form Field Settings > Financials.
3. Click **Type of Funding Settings** (or browse to `/Admin/Field/Section?Section=TypeOfFunding&`).
4. Observe: the section header and column headings render, but the field list is empty (only the Cancel button shows).

## Expected
The editable Type of Funding fields (Amount, Obligation YR, Color/Fiscal YR, Type of Fund, Customer, PWD/MIPR #, P/R Form Contract Award Date, Is Direct, Is Reimbursable) should be listed and clickable so their display name and field settings can be edited — consistent with every other section.

## Root Cause
`FieldController.SetViewbagPropertiesAsync` builds the field list by reflecting only over properties decorated with the `[FieldMetadata]` attribute:
```csharp
var properties = type.GetProperties()
    .Where(x => x.GetCustomAttribute<FieldMetadataAttribute>() != null);
```
`TypeOfFundingViewModel` is the only section view model with **no** `[FieldMetadata]` attributes (its properties carry only `[Display]`/`[Required]`). With zero matching properties, `ViewBag.Properties` is empty and `_PropertiesHelper.cshtml` renders an empty table. The URL and controller routing are correct.

## Proposed Fix
Add `[FieldMetadata(...)]` attributes to the editable fields on `TypeOfFundingViewModel`, mirroring the field set in the Type of Funding edit modal and following the flag conventions used in `ItemFinancialsViewModel` (e.g. `AllowRequired`, `AllowHidden`, `AllowDuplicate`, `AllowLookup` as appropriate per field).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] The Type of Funding settings page lists the editable fields.
- [ ] Each field is clickable into the Edit dialog and its display name can be changed.

issues.title: fix: eliminate tempDB exhaustion from whole-table STRING_AGG in action-list query (PEO_AdjudicationComments)
issues.description:
## Problem

The action-list query (`QueryForList` in `Source/OneNListApp.Service/OneNListItemService.cs`) is exhausting **tempDB in production**, slowly eating up resources under sustained load.

The `PEO_AdjudicationComments` column is sourced from a `FromSqlRaw` derived table:

```sql
SELECT fk_OneNList_ID, STRING_AGG(CAST(UserComments AS NVARCHAR(MAX)), ' | ') AS Comments
FROM dbo.OneNList_PEOAdjudicationComments
GROUP BY fk_OneNList_ID
```

…which is then composed into the projection as a correlated subquery filtered by `fk_OneNList_ID = o.ID`:

```sql
COALESCE((SELECT TOP(1) [o1].[Comments] FROM ( <whole-table GROUP BY above> ) AS [o1]
          WHERE [o1].[fk_OneNList_ID] = [o].[ID]), N'')
```

### Why it destroys tempDB

This is **aggregate-the-whole-table-then-filter** instead of **filter-then-aggregate**:

1. The `WHERE fk_OneNList_ID = o.ID` predicate lives *outside* the grouped aggregate, so SQL Server cannot push it into the derived table.
2. The aggregate is `STRING_AGG(CAST(UserComments AS NVARCHAR(MAX)), ...)` — a **LOB/MAX** aggregation, which forces the GROUP BY into a sort/hash aggregate whose worktable **spills to tempDB**.
3. Because the subquery is correlated, the whole-table LOB aggregation is evaluated **per output row, per page load, per concurrent user**. tempDB grows and is not reclaimed under load.

Every other correlated subquery in the query is safe by comparison: the LookupItem scalars are PK seeks, and the ProjectedObligation/TypeOfFunding aggregations filter *first* (`WHERE fk_OneNList_ID = o.ID`) and aggregate only the action's rows. The comments subquery is the only one that aggregates the full table before filtering.

## Fix (filter-then-aggregate)

Replace the whole-table derived table with a **filter-then-aggregate inline TVF** that scopes the STRING_AGG to a single action:

```sql
CREATE FUNCTION dbo.fnGetPeoAdjudicationCommentsForAction (@onenId int)
RETURNS TABLE
AS RETURN
(
    SELECT STRING_AGG(CAST(UserComments AS NVARCHAR(MAX)), ' | ') AS Comments
    FROM dbo.OneNList_PEOAdjudicationComments
    WHERE fk_OneNList_ID = @onenId
);
```

Map it via `HasDbFunction` (same pattern as `EfSqlFunctions.TryParseFloat`) and compose it in the projection so it becomes an **index seek** aggregating only the action's handful of comment rows — no whole-table scan, no tempDB spill. EF Core 8 still cannot emit `STRING_AGG` from LINQ, so the TVF carries it.

> An inline TVF is preferred over a scalar UDF because the optimizer can inline it; a scalar UDF (`RETURNS NVARCHAR(MAX)`) doing the same filtered STRING_AGG is acceptable if TVF composition proves awkward.

## Files to modify

- `Source/Migrations/5.1.2/08_<date>_AddPeoAdjudicationCommentsForActionTVF.sql` (new) — create `dbo.fnGetPeoAdjudicationCommentsForAction`.
- `Source/OneNListApp.Data/OneNListContext.cs` — map the TVF via `HasDbFunction`; remove the keyless `OneNListPeoAdjudicationCommentsAgg` whole-table registration if no longer used.
- `Source/OneNListApp.Service/OneNListItemService.cs` — delete the `FromSqlRaw` whole-table `peoComments` derived table; compose the filtered TVF call for `PEO_AdjudicationComments` in the projection.
- `Source/OneNListApp.Data/EfSqlFunctions.cs` / TVF stub — add the LINQ-visible mapping method as needed.
- `Source/OneNListApp.IntegrationTests/QueryForListTranslationTests.cs` — regression test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `PEO_AdjudicationComments` is produced by a per-action filtered STRING_AGG (filter-then-aggregate), not a whole-table `GROUP BY` derived table.
- [ ] The SQL generated by `QueryForList(...).ToQueryString()` contains **no** `GROUP BY` over `OneNList_PEOAdjudicationComments` (no whole-table aggregate).
- [ ] The generated SQL references `fnGetPeoAdjudicationCommentsForAction` and filters by `fk_OneNList_ID = [o].[ID]` / `@onenId`.
- [ ] Column output is unchanged: actions with multiple comments return them joined by `' | '`; actions with none return an empty string.
- [ ] Migration script runs cleanly and is idempotent (drop-if-exists guard).
- [ ] Project builds with no errors or warnings.
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass.

## Unit / Integration Test Requirements

Follow the `ToQueryString()` assertion pattern in `QueryForListTranslationTests`:

- `QueryForList_Recent_DoesNotAggregateWholeCommentsTable` — asserts the generated SQL does **not** contain a `GROUP BY` over `OneNList_PEOAdjudicationComments`, and **does** reference `fnGetPeoAdjudicationCommentsForAction` (regression guard so the whole-table pattern cannot creep back).

issues.title: build: upgrade PULSE to .NET 10 (LTS) and align all NuGet packages — freeze Bootstrap 3.3.7 & jQuery 3.7.1
issues.description:
## Summary

Upgrade PULSE from **.NET 8 (LTS)** to **.NET 10 (current LTS, GA Nov 2025)** across the entire solution, and bring all NuGet packages up to their aligned `10.0.x` baselines. This is a single, self-contained platform-maintenance ticket: it keeps PULSE on a supported LTS runtime and eliminates the current cross-project version drift (Data/Service on EF Core 8.0.14, Web on 8.0.18, API mixing EF Core 9.0.1 with classic EntityFramework 6.5.1, `Microsoft.Extensions.*` on 9.0.0).

**The overriding requirement is zero functional regression.** Front-end libraries are the highest-risk area and are handled conservatively:

- **Bootstrap 3.3.7 is FROZEN.** The vendored, PULSE-modified Bootstrap files are **not** to be touched, upgraded, re-minified, or re-fetched. They must be byte-for-byte identical before and after this ticket (verified by checksum — see Guardrails). A Bootstrap major upgrade (3→4/5) is explicitly **out of scope** and, if ever pursued, belongs in its own epic.
- **jQuery stays on 3.7.1** (already the latest 3.x; jQuery 4 is still beta). No jQuery / jQuery UI version change.

This is a server-runtime + NuGet upgrade only. No application behavior, no markup, and no client-side library changes ship in this ticket.

---

## Target versions

| Component | From | To |
|---|---|---|
| .NET SDK (`global.json`) | 8.0.404 / 8.0.414 | latest .NET **10** SDK (10.0.1xx feature band) |
| `TargetFramework` (all 7 projects) | `net8.0` | `net10.0` |
| EF Core (all packages) | 8.0.14 / 8.0.18 / 9.0.1 | **10.0.x** (single unified version) |
| ASP.NET Core packages (DataProtection, Identity.*, SignalR.Client, Authentication.Certificate) | 8.0.x / 9.0.x | **10.0.x** |
| `Microsoft.Extensions.*` | 9.0.0 / 9.0.7 | **10.0.x** |
| Docker base images | `dotnet/aspnet:8.0`, `dotnet/sdk:8.0` | `:10.0` |
| CI runner image | `mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:8.0` | `:10.0` |
| jQuery / jQuery UI | 3.7.1 / 1.13.2 / 1.14.1 | **unchanged** |
| Bootstrap (vendored) | 3.3.7 | **unchanged (frozen)** |

Third-party packages (EPPlus, ClosedXML, X.PagedList, Newtonsoft.Json, StackExchange.Redis, UAParser, Swashbuckle, NSwag, Moq, xunit, Playwright, etc.) should be updated to their current stable releases **only where a `net10.0`-compatible version exists and the change is non-breaking**. Any package whose latest version introduces a breaking API change must be left at its current working version and called out in the MR description rather than force-upgraded.

---

## Files to modify

**SDK / target framework**
- `Source/global.json` — pin to the latest .NET 10 SDK feature band.
- `Source/OneNListApp.Data/global.json` — same .NET 10 SDK pin (remove the drift from the root `global.json`).
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/OneNListApp.Web.csproj` — `net8.0` → `net10.0`; bump EF Core (8.0.18), `Microsoft.AspNetCore.DataProtection` (9.0.7), `Identity.*` (8.0.18), `SignalR.Client` (8.0.18), `Caching.StackExchangeRedis` (9.0.7), `System.Text.Json` (8.0.6) to 10.0.x. **Do not remove** the `<Content Remove>`/`<None Include>` jQuery intellisense entries.
- `Source/OneNListApp.Data/OneNListApp.Data.csproj` — `net8.0` → `net10.0`; unify EF Core (8.0.14 → 10.0.x), `Microsoft.Extensions.*` (9.0.0 → 10.0.x), `Identity.EntityFrameworkCore` (8.0.14 → 10.0.x). Leave `jQuery`/`jQuery.UI.Combined` package refs and the `Content`/`Scripts` items **unchanged**.
- `Source/OneNListApp.Service/OneNListApp.Service.csproj` — `net8.0` → `net10.0`; EF Core 8.0.14 → 10.0.x; `Identity.EntityFrameworkCore` → 10.0.x. Leave jQuery/jQuery UI refs **unchanged**.
- `Source/OneNListApp.API/OneNListApp.API.csproj` — `net8.0` → `net10.0`; EF Core 9.0.1 → 10.0.x. **Investigate the classic `EntityFramework` 6.5.1 reference** — confirm whether it is still used; keep it if so (EF6 runs on .NET 10), document the finding. Bump `Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design` and `Authentication.Certificate` to 10.0.x.
- `Source/OneNListApp.Tests/OneNListApp.Tests.csproj` — `net8.0` → `net10.0`; `EntityFrameworkCore.InMemory` 8.0.0 → 10.0.x (keep the version-unification comment accurate).
- `Source/OneNListApp.IntegrationTests/OneNListApp.IntegrationTests.csproj` — `net8.0` → `net10.0`; EF Core 8.0.14 → 10.0.x.
- `Source/OneNListApp.E2E/OneNListApp.E2E.csproj` — `net8.0` → `net10.0`; update the `playwright.ps1` path comment from `net8.0` to `net10.0`.

**Docker**
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Dockerfile` — `base` (`aspnet:8.0`) and `build` (`sdk:8.0`) stages → `:10.0`.
- `Source/OneNListApp.API/Dockerfile` — `base` (`aspnet:8.0`) and `build` (`sdk:8.0`) stages → `:10.0`.

**CI / publish profiles**
- `Source/pipeline/.gitlab-ci-templates.yml` — `.dotnet-base` image `dotnet/sdk:8.0` → `:10.0`.
- `Source/pipeline/.test-e2e-gitlab-ci.yml` — `playwright.ps1` path `bin/Release/net8.0/` → `net10.0/`.
- `Source/OneNListApp.API/Properties/PublishProfiles/PROD.pubxml` and `QA.pubxml` — `<TargetFramework>net8.0</TargetFramework>` → `net10.0`.
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/Properties/PublishProfiles/FolderProfile.pubxml` — `net8.0` → `net10.0`.

**Docs (text references only)**
- `README.md`, `docs/PULSE-Build-and-Deployment.md`, `docs/LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.md`, `Source/OneNListApp.API/ReadMe/README.md` — update `.NET 8` / `net8.0` references to `.NET 10`.

**Explicitly NOT modified (frozen):**
- `Source/OneNListApp.Web/wwwroot/css/bootstrap*.css` (+ `.map`), `Source/OneNListApp.Web/wwwroot/scripts/bootstrap.js` / `bootstrap.min.js`, `bootstrap-multiselect.*`, and all `jquery-*` / `jquery-ui-*` script files. `libman.json` and `bundleconfig.json` remain unchanged.

---

## Guardrails / anti-regression protections

1. **Bootstrap byte-for-byte freeze.** Before starting, record SHA-256 checksums of every `wwwroot/css/bootstrap*` and `wwwroot/scripts/bootstrap*` + `jquery*` file. After the upgrade, re-compute and confirm the hashes are identical. Any diff fails the ticket. Do **not** run `libman restore`, `dotnet bundle`, or any minifier step that would regenerate `site.min.css` / `site.min.js` from changed inputs.
2. **One concern per commit.** Sequence the work so a regression can be bisected: (a) `global.json` + all `TargetFramework` bumps; (b) EF Core unification; (c) remaining ASP.NET Core / Extensions package bumps; (d) Docker + CI + pubxml; (e) docs. Build and run the full test suite after each step.
3. **EF Core upgrade is the highest server-side risk.** EF Core 10 changes some query translation and default behaviors. After the EF bump, run `OneNListApp.IntegrationTests` against a real SQL Server (the SP→EF `#675` translation tests: permission-TVF IN-subquery, `STRING_AGG`, fiscal-year aggregation, `OFFSET/FETCH` paging) — the InMemory provider cannot catch these. Generate no new migrations unless the model changed (it must not in this ticket).
4. **No new analyzer warnings.** `net10.0` enables newer analyzers; the build must remain warning-clean. Address (or explicitly justify) any new warnings rather than suppressing globally.
5. **Verify the classic `EntityFramework` 6.5.1 / `System.ServiceModel.Http` / `System.Linq 4.3.0` legacy refs** still resolve and run on .NET 10 before declaring done.
6. **Smoke-test the running app** (`InfrastructureSmokeTests` + manual): login, list/index, item create/edit, admin lookup screens, Excel import/export, SignalR notifications, and Data Protection key persistence (antiforgery tokens) — these touch the upgraded packages most directly.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `global.json` (both files) pin the latest .NET 10 SDK; `dotnet --version` resolves to 10.x on the build host.
- [ ] All 7 projects target `net10.0`; solution builds in Debug **and** QA/PROD configurations with **no errors and no new warnings**.
- [ ] EF Core is a single unified `10.0.x` version across Web, Data, Service, API, Tests, and IntegrationTests (no remaining 8.0.x / 9.0.1 EF Core references).
- [ ] `Microsoft.Extensions.*` and all ASP.NET Core packages are on `10.0.x`; no mixed major versions remain.
- [ ] Both Dockerfiles build against `dotnet/sdk:10.0` / `dotnet/aspnet:10.0`; the Web and API images run and serve `/PULSE/Health` (and the API root) successfully.
- [ ] CI pipeline (`.gitlab-ci-templates.yml`) builds and the unit-test job passes on the `:10.0` runner image; the E2E job's `playwright.ps1` path resolves under `net10.0`.
- [ ] Publish profiles (`PROD.pubxml`, `QA.pubxml`, `FolderProfile.pubxml`) target `net10.0` and a self-contained `win-x64` publish succeeds.
- [ ] **Bootstrap and jQuery/jQuery UI vendored files are byte-for-byte unchanged** (verified by checksum); `site.min.css` / `site.min.js` are not regenerated.
- [ ] Full unit-test suite (`OneNListApp.Tests`) passes; `OneNListApp.IntegrationTests` passes against real SQL Server (or skips cleanly when DB is unreachable).
- [ ] `OneNListApp.E2E` Playwright suite passes against the upgraded stack.
- [ ] Manual smoke test passes: login, list, item create/edit, admin lookup, Excel import/export, SignalR, antiforgery/Data Protection.
- [ ] Project builds with no errors or warnings after the change.
- [ ] All existing tests continue to pass.

## Unit Test Requirements

No new application logic is introduced, so no new unit tests are required. Verification is via the **existing** suites run on the upgraded framework: `OneNListApp.Tests` (unit), `OneNListApp.IntegrationTests` (real-SQL EF translation), and `OneNListApp.E2E` (Playwright). `InfrastructureSmokeTests` must pass on `net10.0` as the baseline build/DI sanity check.
